correctness.rationale: The numerator minus denominator factors as the product of the three input differences from 1; their sum is the product of their sums with 1 plus 2b. This gives exactly the specified Cayley map, never creates a zero from an admissible history, and gives nonnegative forcing bounded by log(1+2b). Entrywise U_0 dominates a positive multiple of the Perron right eigenvector, so u_n is bounded below by that multiple of rho^n. Smoothness of the forcing on the resulting small Cayley inputs gives the stated super-exponential bound. The shift by c/2 and the left/right eigenprojectors give the exact finite variation-of-constants formula; in the omitted tail, the factor |t|^(-j-1) at k=n+j is dominated by the geometric decay obtained from rho^j >= 1+j(rho-1), even for the stable pair. Unshifted Perron projection gives the positive amplitude and its bounds; dominated convergence with epsilon_k(b)/b <= 2 gives the right derivative at fixed history and strict positivity. For the claimed possible growth, at b=0 choose a positive Perron initial vector plus a small real part of a lambda eigenvector. This is realizable by an admissible history and gives a nonzero growing oscillatory envelope (two successive cosines cannot both tend to zero). Conversion to log|z_n-1| adds log 2 plus a super-exponentially small correction. An exact initial zero propagates by the primitive lag graph, consistently outside the logarithmic statement.
